notes.decision: '(in their) deviance.' Compound: Greek prefix ⲡⲁⲣⲁ- ('alongside, contrary to') + ⲡⲉⲥⲟⲩⲧ (= ⲥⲟⲩⲧⲱⲛ 'straight, upright') + ⲙⲛⲧ- abstract = 'state-of-being-alongside-the-straight' = 'crookedness, deviance, heresy.' Distinguishes the heretics' system from the upright way.

'The interpretation of the five sayings.' ⲡⲃⲱⲗ here is the substantive form of ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'release/loose' = 'release-of-meaning' = 'interpretation,' parallel to ⲍⲉⲣⲙⲏⲛⲓⲁ in earlier vocab. ⲥⲉⲭⲉ = ϣⲁϫⲉ 'word, saying.'
Repeated 'ⲓⲃ̄' (12) at start and end of heading line preserved literally. Likely a paragraph-marker or scribal numeration framing the chapter heading.
Read as Lycopolitan reflex of πάλιν 'again' with prosthetic ⲧ-. Standard discourse marker introducing dialogue with the disciples.
'The Pure Ones' (καθάριος). Self-designation of the Baptists / Mandaean-type baptizing groups whom Manichaeans critique. Preserves the technical Greek term as a sect-name.
'The unnameable.' ⲁⲧ- (privative) + ϯ-ⲣⲉⲛ ('give-name') + ⲁⲣⲁϩ ('to him') = 'the one to whom no name is given' = the unnameable Father. Cf. ϯⲡⲉⲛ in earlier vocab — Lyc. ⲡⲉⲛ for ⲣⲉⲛ.

Tentatively 'of his name' with ⲧⲛⲉⲥ as a noun (possibly ⲧⲱⲛⲥ 'foundation, establishment' or related to 'image/figure'). The end of one heretical saying transitioning to the second. Confidence low pending parallels.

Rendered 'whom they themselves call' — ⲍⲱϩ (Lyc. = ϩⲱⲱϥ, intensive/reflexive 'himself/itself') here intensifies the calling. Could also be construed 'whom they call upon him as well.' The 'Father of [...]' formula is a standard divine titulature.

Tentatively read as a Lycopolitan/scribal variant of ⲡⲟⲩⲣⲟ/ⲡⲟⲣⲟ 'the king.' The phrase ⲡⲟⲃⲣⲟ ⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲱⲛ ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲛⲉ ('the king of the aeons of light') fits standard Manichaean phraseology for the Father of Greatness. ⲡⲟⲣⲟ is well-attested in vocab; the -ⲃ- here is unusual and may reflect dialectal vocalization or scribal slip.
Lexeme on papyrus but unidentified. Plural noun, object of ⲁⲥⲑⲃⲟ 'she humbled.' Held in the line as preserved Coptic with note rather than as lacuna.
'they are one body, living' — ⲉϩⲁⲛⲍ = ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ 'living' (qualitative). Captures the Manichaean unity-of-life motif: all things together constitute one Living Body.
